subject: Connection strategy survey: Private VPC / access model
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Subject: Connection strategy survey: Private VPC / access model

Hi Laura — great to meet earlier today. Quick post-call recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the Private VPC option properly and prep a short network playbook for your NetSec team.

Recap (very short):
- Your team wants isolated hosting for production models and data residency in us-west.
- Primary constraint: security team requires no public-facing egress without approved static IPs.
- Preferred timeline: pilot in Q1 with full rollout in Q2.

To size the solution and recommend a connection approach (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs customer-managed reverse-proxy), can you confirm the following items? If easier, reply inline.

Quick survey:
1) Intended network ownership for egress: will Nimbus manage NAT/eSIP (customer-managed egress) or do you want Redwood to provide static egress IPs and manage outbound? (answer: customer / redwood)
2) Do you have mandated CIDR blocks we must peer into? If yes, include primary CIDR and whether there are multiple VPCs.
3) Any blocking firewall rules (deny-by-default) that require specific ports open for health checks?
4) Will NetSec accept cross-account VPC peering, or must we use PrivateLink endpoints?
5) Desired maintenance window and on-call contact for peering setup (name, email, timezone).

Attachments: deployment_options_onepager.pdf — high-level comparison (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and rough network diagrams.

Next steps from Redwood: once you reply with the items above we will:
- Draft a connectivity recommendation and a minimal IP/port checklist for your firewall team.
- Schedule a 60-min NetOps working session (we'll propose slots).

Thanks — copying Ben and Marissa so they can prep pricing and the technical sketch.

Best,

Jasmine Liu

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the recap and the one-pager.

Answers inline:
1) Egress ownership: We prefer to keep egress within our VPC (customer-managed NAT) but we need static IPs for a handful of downstream partners. If Redwood can offer static egress IPs as an option, that would be good to know.
2) CIDRs: Primary VPC CIDR is 10.10.0.0/16. We also have a security VPC at 10.20.0.0/24 that might need access.
3) Firewall: NetSec is deny-by-default. They'll need explicit IP/port lists. Health checks should be over TCP on 443 and a small management TCP port 15001 (for readiness probes) — confirm if Redwood requires anything else.
4) Peering vs PrivateLink: NetSec typically prefers peering for internal services, but they have stricter rules for cross-account access. They may request PrivateLink if we cannot provide an audit trail for peering.
5) Maintenance window / contact: mornings 09:00-12:00 PST. Primary network lead: Carlos Vega <c.vega@nimbusfin.com>.

I've attached our security questionnaire (partial) so NetSec has context. We can join a working session next week on Tue/Wed morning.

Laura Mitchell
Director, Platform Security | Nimbus Financial
laura@nimbusfin.com

Thanks — this is super helpful, Laura. Quick clarifications and recommended next steps below.

Short answers:
- Static egress IPs: Redwood can provide an egress proxy option that presents static IPs back to your partners (this is a managed add-on). If you want to keep egress customer-managed, we'll peer into your VPC and expect outbound to go through your NAT.
- Health checks/ports: For peering mode we need outbound TCP 443 and for runtime health checks TCP 15001 as you noted; additionally we will request ephemeral TCP 1024-65535 for ephemeral connections when debugging — those are optional and can be restricted.
- Peering vs PrivateLink: High-level tradeoffs — peering gives lower latency and fewer hops (recommended if both sides accept cross-account peering). PrivateLink provides stronger isolation and avoids cross-account routing changes (recommended if NetSec prohibits peering). We'll include both options in the playbook.

What we need from your side to prepare the playbook and the network diagram:
- Confirm final list of VPC CIDRs (you already provided primary + security VPC; indicate any other connected VPCs).
- Provide Carlos's contact so we can set an invite for the NetOps workshop (best: calendar invite with a short preread).
- If you prefer Redwood-managed egress, say so and we'll include pricing + SLA notes for static IPs.

Attached: redwood_vpc_peering_sketch.png (simple sketch showing peer vs endpoint and where static egress would sit). Also linking a short Drive folder with templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleLink

Proposed slots for a 60-min NetOps working session:
- Tue 2027-12-21 09:30 PST
- Wed 2027-12-22 10:00 PST

If those work I’ll send an invite and Marissa will bring the prefilled checklist for your firewall team.

Best,

Quick technical notes from infra — we can cover in the workshop but logging them here so NetSec can review ahead: 
- Ports: TCP 443 (recommended), TCP 15001 (readiness), ICMP allowed only for troubleshooting (optional).
- Peering: we require: (a) route table entries for the Redwood-allocated prefixes, (b) no overlapping CIDRs, and (c) IGW/NAT set up on the Nimbus side if you plan to egress through your NAT.
- PrivateLink: will require an NLB in our account and a VPC endpoint in yours; we’ll provide the NLB IPs and certificate info ahead of time.
- DNS: if you want service discovery via private DNS, we’ll need the zone details and whether you allow us to write private-host records.

Short checklist (for your firewall):
- Allow inbound from Redwood peering CIDR: 100.64.0.0/18 (example; final to be provided).
- Allow outbound to Redwood health-check endpoint on 15001/TCP.
- If using Redwood-managed egress, allow egress to partners on the static IP set we’ll provide.

I’ll join the working session; happy to review route tables and do a quick connectivity test in-session.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
